note: Contrarian Shark, competitor angle only. Judged solely against the North Star and the draft text as written. Findings press where a rival product or a rival “ship honest UX first” team would beat this plan on the same North Star.

findings.criterion: 1’s narrower “Retry, Diagnose, restart” success-criteria wording. That wording itself under-specifies the North Star’s leading verbs and must be expanded or the missing waves added.
findings.message: The North Star leads with four verbs — open, run, stop, restart. The plan’s Phase-3 surface train covers attach, usage/time, cost, Doctor, stop-summary, restart, preview, projects-collapse, and cadence. There is no surface wave that owns **open** or **run** as first-class controls (dead-control contract, named cannot-*, failure-state table, e2e trace). W1 only records a task triple that *includes* open/run as human confirmation items; nothing later forces those controls to work or be hidden. A competitor that ships the full work loop would treat open and run as load-bearing product surfaces, not ambient preconditions. As written, the build can go GREEN on stop/restart/attach while open/run remain dead or silent — and still claim the North Star via S1 partial pass or

findings.section: Waves 8–19 gate-commands; W9 trace schema; Success criteria “works end-to-end”
findings.criterion: Every surface that claims health, usage, or diagnose either works end-to-end or fails with a named, user-visible state
findings.message: Every surface wave’s “e2e” is `generate_html` / visible-text-node assertions plus `node --check` on script blocks, with a JSON “control→handler→capability→state” trace. That is unit-level render theater, not a user path. A competitor product proves end-to-end by driving the real UI (click Diagnose, attach from the session list, open a .docx, stop a live session) against a real or high-fidelity Anchor process and asserting the live DOM/state. This plan can pass every scoped pytest while the real control remains unbound in the served app, the click never reaches the handler, or the preview path only works in the fixture harness. “Works end-to-end” in the North Star is a user claim; HTML-string GREEN is a competitor’s favorite false green. Require at least one real interaction path per North-Star surface (or an honest named degradation if the host cannot automate UI), not only rendered-string conformance.

findings.criterion: without meeting a dead control … Doctor diagnose and session attach … works end-to-end or fails with a named, user-visible state
findings.message: W3 freezes PRESENT/STUB/ABSENT from “captured-once, replayed-many” transcripts so John is not needed live. A competitor inventory re-probes the live v1.2 surface (or fails closed to unknown) at freeze and again before each surface wave GO. One-shot replay lets a control go PRESENT on an old transcript while the real handler is now a no-op, canned, or unbound — then W13–W16 “wire it / build it” decisions and dead-control audits inherit a lie. That is exactly how dead Diagnose/Retry/restart survive a “capability-backed” plan. Capture-once is fine for offline unit tests; it is illegal as the sole authority for PRESENT that authorizes shipping a live control. Either re-probe at freeze + pre-surface GO, or treat aged transcripts as unknown and force re-inventory — never PRESENT-by-replay alone.

findings.section: Wave 11 (E2 as_of provisional usage/time); Wave 2 E2 rules; Success criteria usage/time/cost
findings.criterion: silent zero … unknown ≠ empty ≠ zero … Cost never fabricates dollars (and usage surfaces that claim numbers must not fabricate confidence)
findings.message: Cost correctly bans E2 and fabricated dollars. Usage/time still allow a signed E2 “provisional” count with an as_of stamp. A competitor usage surface never shows a numeral until the rollup is PROVEN; provisional is still a confident wrong answer — the defect class the honesty gate names. An as_of stamp next to a wrong count is a disclaimer, not honesty. If the rollup is UNPROVEN, the only competitive-grade states are pending/unknown/measurement_failed — not a number under E2. Close E2 for any user-visible count that criterion 3 surfaces (usage and time), or the plan institutionalizes silent-wrong (cousin of silent zero) on half of the usage/time/cost criterion while being strict only on dollars.

findings.section: Wave 13 done-when / GWT; criterion 4 Doctor real diagnose
findings.criterion: including Doctor diagnose … real diagnose (success criteria: Doctor real diagnose; banner payload)
findings.message: W13’s proof that diagnosis is “real” is: two induced faults produce *different* rendered findings. A competitor Doctor is real when findings track injected root causes with structured, checkable claims (and non-canned content), not when two templates differ. Seeded multi-branch theater still “differs” and still fails the North Star’s “real diagnose.” Require fault→expected finding contracts (or inventory-backed golden transcripts of real diagnose behavior), plus an explicit ban on fixed seed strings — variance alone is a competitor-beatable bar.

findings.section: Success criteria; Wave 13 banner_handoff; North Star “health, usage, or diagnose”
findings.criterion: 4/health to every health-claiming surface, or the plan closes “diagnose” while leaving health claims free to silent-zero and mislabelled-empty.
findings.message: Usage and diagnose get full surface trains; “health” is reduced to banner→Doctor payload handoff. There is no wave that inventories every surface that *claims* health (banner copy, health tile, status chrome) and forces ok/unknown/empty/zero_measured/failed with unknown≠empty. A competitor health strip that shows green/empty/zero without evidence loses users to an honest unknown. Expand

findings.section: Wave 3 STUB→build it; Wave 5 DOC-TRIO-AMENDMENT / WAVE-LIST-FREEZE
findings.criterion: open/run/stop/restart + Doctor + attach without dead controls; surfaces work E2E or named failure
findings.message: The competitive product scopes “build it vs wire it” before committing the surface train. This plan discovers STUBs in W3, then relies on mid-build wave insertion and re-freeze. That is honest process, but it leaves the delivered North Star set unbounded: enough STUBs and the conjunction scorer (2-per-criterion / 4 total) or schedule pressure pushes E1/E3 exits or dropped surfaces. Competitor plans either (a) pre-budget a fixed maximum of build-it waves with explicit cut-line to named unavailable states, or (b) inventory before freeze with a hard cap on unsigned STUBs. Without a hard scope/cut-line tied to the ten criteria, “freeze then amend forever” is how dead controls become signed exits or unshipped work while process stays GREEN.

findings.section: Wave 1 task triple; Wave 21 S1; Steward/S1 North Star clause
findings.criterion: open, run, stop, restart … Doctor diagnose and session attach; Steward conversational proof is a post-build validation session (S1), not a silent claim of this build
findings.message: S1-as-sole North Star declaration is correct and must stay. Competitor *engineering* still re-runs the verification task triple (or an automated subset) after each surface wave that claims a verb in that triple — attach after W10, diagnose after W13/W14, stop/restart after W15/W16 — so failures are cheap and early. This plan explicitly avoids live John until S1 and relies on fixture/fault injection in between. That maximizes late BUILD_BLOCKING discovery after twenty waves of process and partial product. Keep S1 as the only *declaration* of North Star met; add mandatory mid-build task-triple checkpoints (or host-automated equivalents) so “not a silent claim” is not paired with “first real user proof is also the last.”

findings.topic: nine infra waves before any surface fix
findings.criterion: On branch v1.2, John can open, run, stop, and restart … without meeting a dead control, a silent zero, a mislabelled empty, or a preview that dumps raw binary
findings.message: A competitor team ships the smallest honest product first: named-state primitive + the dead controls John hits daily (Diagnose, Retry/attach, restart, binary preview). This plan serializes nine Phase-0/1/2 waves (task triple, exit register, inventory, rollup gate, freeze, named state, cost_state, conformance harness, trace/fault/log) before any Phase-3 surface can start, then serializes surfaces through W19. The machinery serves honesty, but the critical path maximizes calendar risk that S1 fails or exits accumulate. Competitor sequencing: W6-class named state + one or two highest-pain surfaces in parallel with inventory/rollup, freeze only what those surfaces need. As written, the plan optimizes for process completeness over competitive time-to-honest-UX on the North Star’s daily path.

findings.section: Wave 17 File preview; Wave 3 inventory “preview path”
findings.criterion: a preview that dumps raw binary … File preview human-friendly Office/PDF via shared path
findings.message: W17 “reuses the already-working new-window renderer.” That is a competitor foot-gun: if the shared path is STUB, format-incomplete, or only works for one type, the wave becomes a thin router over a broken dependency and binary can still appear on alternate code paths. Inventory must prove PRESENT per format (docx/pptx/xlsx/pdf) with transcripts of human-friendly output *before* W17 is allowed to claim reuse; if STUB, W17 is a build-it wave for the renderer itself, not a wire-up. Competitor products do not ship “delegate to shared path” without per-format evidence the path actually humanizes those bytes.

findings.section: Wave 21 release_guard.py; North Star v1.1.x clause; Wave 1 containment
findings.criterion: Nothing in this effort ships to v1.1.x collaborators
findings.message: Containment smoke protects planning-path writes and root foreign Foreman artifacts; the only explicit “not publishable to v1.1.x” guard is W21. A competitor release process fails closed on branch/channel from the first product commit (W6+). Late-only release_guard allows accidental packaging, tag, or channel bleed during surface waves. Move branch/channel non-publish checks to an early always-on gate (or extend W1 containment to publish surfaces), not only the terminal wave.

findings.topic: restart dual-control audit is HTML count only
findings.criterion: exactly one restart control per restart context — work or not shown; no dual competing controls
findings.message: The audit asserts control count == 1 in rendered HTML. A competitor also proves behavioral exclusivity: only one control can trigger restart for that context (no hidden keyboard path, menu duplicate, or second entry point that restarts with a different preserved/lost contract). Count-of-buttons GREEN with two behavioral restart paths still violates “exactly one restart control per context.” Extend the contract to “exactly one restart *action* per context,” not only one labelled button in the HTML snapshot.

findings.topic: failure-state vocabulary mismatched to UI surfaces
findings.section: Hardening-gate obligations Failure-state table vocabulary; Waves 10–19 failure-states/*
findings.criterion: unknown ≠ empty ≠ zero; named, user-visible state
findings.message: The emitted 0080 vocabulary (dependency-missing, index read/write, rebuild, reconcile, verify, CLI verbs) reads like a storage/index product, not Anchor session/Doctor/cost UI. Wave-local tables partially re-map, but the plan still requires those five rows “per surface (index read/write…).” A competitor names the states the *user* hits (attach timeout, unmeasured cost, inventory unreadable, unsupported preview). If agents fill index-reconcile rows for a Doctor tile, honesty theater returns. Require surface-native failure rows that map 1:1 to NamedState/user-visible strings for each North-Star surface; keep storage vocabulary only where the surface actually is a store/CLI.
